per_layer_decision_rationale.worker_2_activity_toxicity: Rebuilt the missing activity layer with four primary-source PvD1 anti-Leishmania proliferation-inhibition records: 300 ug/ml at 24 and 48 h and 600 ug/ml at 24 and 48 h. Each row has endpoint, value, unit, concentration, target species/strain/stage, assay conditions, and XML/PDF/Figure 1 locators. No toxicity or hemolysis row was fabricated because this paper does not report one locally.

The DBAASP 300 ug/ml / 70% Leishmania assertion matches the primary source activity row, but exact peptide sequence identity is absent from this current paper and linked_sequence_records is empty, so those assay/experiment rows remain source_conflict with context rather than source_verified. The dbAMP mixed entry is preserved as source_conflict because only its Leishmania assertion is supported by this DOI.

adjudication_summary: Source-reviewed re-review repaired doi__10.1042_bsr20150060 by extracting the primary anti-Leishmania activity rows, preserving database identity/mixed-entry conflicts as cautions, and bounding mechanism claims to the assays actually present. The paper is publication-grade with cautions, not clean acceptance.

caution_findings.note: Primary activity, concentration, target, and citation are supported; exact PvD1 amino-acid sequence identity is not present in the current local primary paper or linked sequence snapshot.
The dbAMP entry mixes multiple publication-linked target strings. This paper supports only the Leishmania 300 ug/ml / 70% inhibition assertion, so other targets were not promoted as primary evidence.
The local primary source supports proliferation inhibition but does not report hemolysis/cytotoxicity rows for this paper.
Membrane permeabilization and TEM morphology are direct assay-backed; intracellular localization is retained as context, not a named molecular target.
The packet status remains material_extracted_with_gaps from the message-transfer run, but local source review found no supplementary assets and closed the analysis blocker.
